title: Introduce microbatch coordinator, NUMA-aware KV sharding, and dependency upgrades
creator: Ava Chen
description: Refactor the continuous batching runtime by introducing an explicit microbatch coordinator that separates admission, packing, and execution stages. Make KV-cache sharding NUMA-aware to reduce cross-socket memory traffic, and perform a coordinated upgrade of runtime dependencies (async runtime and async-io libraries) required by the new async pipeline. This aims to reduce tail latency on high-concurrency tenants, lower CPU migration overhead, and remove fragile coupling between admission and execution paths.
acceptance_criteria: New microbatch coordinator implemented behind feature flag and can be toggled at shard-level
KV-cache shard allocator is NUMA-aware and shows reduced cross-socket allocations in perf traces
End-to-end benchmarks show 20% median p99 reduction for 99th-percentile tail latency for high-concurrency synthetic workload (>=2000 rps per model)
All unit/integration tests updated and passing in CI; canary rollout executed on dedicated pool with rollback playbook
Dependency upgrades (async runtime and async-io crate) merged and no new security alerts in SCA scan

notes: We chose a microbatch coordinator instead of refactoring the existing continuous-batcher to minimize risk to the legacy path; coordinator can be opt-in per shard.
NUMA-aware allocator uses a simple socket-local freelist and prefers local shard placement for hot keys; fallback to global when local resources exhausted.
Upgrading async runtime required small API adaptors in existing io adapters; migration notes captured in the design doc.
Memory-safety review scheduled with Security team due to allocator changes and dependency bumps.
We intentionally avoid changing kernel-level io (libaio) in this ticket; if further gains required we'll schedule separate ticket for aio path optimization.
